name: Wrap a gift professionally
blurb: Crisp corners, hidden tape and a proper bow. It takes ten minutes to learn the diagonal fold that makes the ends look shop-wrapped.
gear: Good-quality paper — thin paper tears at the corners
steps: Measure the paper properly: enough to overlap by about 3 cm around the box, and just over half the box depth at each end.
Fold a crisp hem on the overlapping edge so no raw cut edge shows, and use double-sided tape underneath so no tape is visible.
For the ends, push the sides in first to form two triangular flaps, crease them sharply, then fold the top flap down and the bottom flap up.
Crease every fold hard with a fingernail or a ruler. Sharp creases are the difference between wrapped and bundled.
Learn a proper ribbon wrap with the cross underneath, and a bow that sits flat.
Learn one alternative for awkward shapes: a fabric furoshiki wrap or a bag with tissue.
tips: Thin cheap paper tears exactly at the corner you care about. Buy heavier paper.
Double-sided tape is the single biggest upgrade to how wrapping looks.
proof: A wrapped box with sharp corners, no visible tape and a flat bow.
